newsitem.title: JAPAN: KDD, AT&T close to deal on cutting overseas costs.
newsitem.headline: KDD, AT&T close to deal on cutting overseas costs.

text.p: Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd KDN1 said on Friday it was close to an agreement with AT&T Corp on a steep cut in rates KDD charges the American company to complete calls from the United States.
The cuts could eventually reduce the costs of foreign calls Americans make to Japan by saving huge sums that U.S. phone companies pay to their Japanese counterparts.
A KDD spokesman said the negotiations with AT&T were continuing, but added that the rates AT&T pays to KDD could be down to nearly one-third the current level of 52 yen per minute.
"It would be eventually close to the benchmark prices the U.S. government proposed last year," he told Reuters.

Last December, the U.S. Federal Communications Commission said the charges American phone companies pay to their foreign counterparts were too high compared with actual costs and proposed "benchmarks" to try to push down the so-called "settlement rates" levied to complete U.S.-originated calls.
Under the proposal, the upper limit would be 15 cents per minute for high-income countries such as Japan.
But the spokesman said the expected cut was the result of three years of talks with AT&T, not the FCC's proposal.
If agreement is reached, KDD will apply to Japan's Posts and Telecommunications Ministry for approval for a rate cut as early as April, he said.
The settlement fees would be reduced in steps to the target rates by April 1998.
The new rates would also be adopted by other Japanese and American telephone companies, and would be implemented dating back to April 1996, he said.
The rate cut would somewhat reduce KDD's profits, a spokeswoman said without elaborating.
The FCC has said that U.S. carriers must pay 46 cents a minute to have their calls connected to Japan even though the actual cost is less than six cents a minute.
